title: UPI Merchant Fee Rollout May Be Deferred to January 2027 Amid Retailer Pushback
excerpt: Less than a week before the 0.40% UPI merchant fee was due to begin, retailers and fintech firms are pressing NPCI to delay it until January 2027 — and a decision is expected within days.
body:
• The 0.40% UPI merchant discount rate on person-to-merchant payments above ₹2,000 — due to start October 15 — may be deferred to January 1, 2027, with a final decision expected in the coming days, according to Business Standard.
  • NPCI’s UPI and Services Steering Committee is also weighing an exemption for businesses with annual turnover of up to ₹40 lakh, sharply expanding the earlier ₹1-lakh-a-month small-merchant carve-out.
  • Markets moved on the news: Paytm shares fell 7.6% and Mobikwik 7.2% on October 8 after CNBC-TV18 reported the possible delay, Reuters reported.
  • What this means for you: nothing changes for consumers — UPI payments stay free, and the charge (if it comes) falls on merchants, not users. If you run a shop in India taking UPI payments above ₹2,000, watch for NPCI’s decision before the festive-season rush.

India may hold off on charging merchants for UPI payments until next year. Days before the 0.40% merchant discount rate (MDR) was due to take effect, merchant bodies, fintechs, and payments companies asked the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to delay it until January 2027 — and a decision could come within days.

Context & Background

The framework would end the zero-MDR era that has defined UPI since its launch. Under the announced structure, a 0.40% charge would apply to eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction. Specified categories — bill payments, utilities, education, and fuel — would carry a flat ₹5 per transaction above ₹2,000. Payments up to ₹2,000, person-to-person transfers, and small-merchant transactions would remain exempt, and consumers would not pay anything.

https://x.com/yatinmota/status/2108042572769984658

Parliament’s Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed in August, empowered NPCI’s steering committee to set an MDR; NPCI confirmed the 0.40% structure in September. The Centre has told the Supreme Court that around 96% of merchant transactions would remain unaffected, putting the covered share at about 4%.

The acquiring bank collects MDR from the merchant and passes 0.28% to the issuing bank as interchange, which routes 0.12% to the payer-side bank and 0.08% to the UPI app provider — the first real UPI revenue stream for banks and apps.

Impact & Analysis

The pushback has been loud. The All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA) and the All India Consumer Products Distributors Federation (AICPDF) called for a “No UPI Day” on October 2, withdrawing the protest only after meeting Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on September 30. AIMRA wants a fixed, nominal charge instead of the 0.40% rate; AICPDF estimates the fee could add ₹7,000 crore to ₹9,000 crore in annual costs across the FMCG distribution and retail ecosystem.

The Retailers Association of India warns the fee would push small merchants back toward cash. “Small merchants will now think twice about whether to accept cash or UPI. During the festive season, a large share of transactions crosses the Rs 2,000 mark, and the moment a fee attaches itself to digital payment, cash becomes the path of least resistance,” CEO Kumar Rajagopalan told PTI. Retailers argue bank-to-bank UPI payments should not be priced like credit cards, and that the state — not merchants — should fund the network.

“Small merchants will now think twice about whether to accept cash or UPI. During the festive season, a large share of transactions crosses the Rs 2,000 mark, and the moment a fee attaches itself to digital payment, cash becomes the path of least resistance.”

— Kumar Rajagopalan, CEO, Retailers Association of India

The sharpest pressure point is timing: the government fears higher payment costs could weaken consumer sentiment ahead of the festive season, sources told Moneycontrol. Investors see it too: the delay reports pushed Paytm down 7.6% and Mobikwik 7.2% on October 8, since the fee was expected to open a new revenue stream from merchant transactions that were previously free.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, the mechanics are unchanged: the fee falls on Indian merchants, not payers, so NRIs using UPI during visits to India — or through its acceptance in more than 10 countries — pay nothing extra. But the dispute matters to anyone watching India’s digital-payments model: a decade of zero-fee UPI was state-subsidized, and who funds its next phase will shape how sustainable — and how global — the system becomes.

What’s Next

NPCI is discussing the deferral request with the finance ministry, and a decision is expected in the coming days — with the October 15 start date less than a week away. Alongside the timing question, the committee is weighing the ₹40-lakh-turnover exemption and a possible rise in the daily UPI limit for certain categories from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh. Whether the fee lands in January or later, the harder questions — stopping merchants from passing the charge to customers, and keeping small retailers on the digital network — will outlast the start date.
